newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 28.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- EX-SPY BOSS GOES OVER TO MARKS

Former MI5 director-general Dame Stella Rimington has joined the board of Marks & Spencer as a part-time director. She will take up the position in January 1997, replacing former Cabinet member Baroness Young.
-- HOUSE OF FRASER FINANCE DIRECTOR DEPARTS

Troubled department store group House of Fraser announced that finance director Richard Scott had left the company. He was the second of two long-standing executive directors to leave since John Coleman replaced Andrew Jennings following the March profits warning.
-- TATE & LYLE SOURED BY CORN PRICE SURGE

Sugar producer Tate & Lyle's profits dropped 11 percent last year after corn prices doubled, hitting the profits from its American sweeteners and starch business, Staley. Pre-tax profits fell from 311 million pounds stg to 276 million pounds.
THE TIMES
-- ALLIANCE & LEICESTER BOARD MAY DROP FLOTATION PLAN

Following an Alliance & Leicester board meeting, the building society could drop of it's proposed 2.5 billion pounds stg flotation. The UK's fourth largest building society has received legal advice that its transfer document, already sent to 3.5 million savers and borrowers, may contain misleading information if a planned new Building Societies Bill is published.
-- SFO AND POLICE LAUNCH INQUIRY OVER WICKES

A formal investigation has been launched by the Serious Fraud Office and the Metropolitan Police into the former senior management of Wickes, the DIY retailer, over a 51 million pounds stg overstatement of past profits. Since the overstatement, disclosed last June, several senior executives have left the company. The present management of Wickes is co-operating fully with the investigation.
-- SIR ROCCO CHECKS BACK INTO HOTEL TRADE AT 12 MILLION POUNDS

Sir Rocco Forte is to return to the hotel business with plans for a 12-million-pound stg luxury hotel in Cardiff. The proposed 120-bed hotel, will be the first five-star standard hotel in Wales and will be on a promontory in Cardiff Bay. It should be completed in 1999.
THE GUARDIAN
-- LEGAL THREAT TO KEEP GAS FLOWING

British Gas has taken emergency steps to ensure the supply of gas to homes throughout winter after pipeline business TransCo revealed it had come close to a transmission breakdown. Steps include the threat of criminal prosecution of large firms who refuse to shut down gas-fired plants when ordered to do so. -- STRONG EXPORTS NARROW TRADE GAP

Britain's trade gap with Europe has hit a three-year low, according to the Office of National Statistics. Exporters have forced the figures down with aggressive selling in France and Germany despite the strong pound.
-- SAFEWAY BANKS ON CUSTOMER BONUS

Safeway will today announce a payment card in association with Abbey National, to be launched in the Spring. The card will be the start of a joint venture eventually leading to jointly branded savings accounts in the wake of similar ventures by Tesco and Sainsbury.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- CLARKE FACES TRIPLE BUDGET BACKLASH

Economists yesterday criticised Kenneth Clarke's Budget, even after the Chancellor claimed to have been more prudent than commentators had expected. Economists were particularly outraged by the way the sales of the student loan book and Ministry of Defence housing were classed, not as privatisation revenue but offset against the departmental spending programmes. This departure from convention allowed the Treasury to the state the Control Total as around 2 billion pounds stg lower next year than it would have been. Analysts also doubted the crackdown on tax avoidance and social security fraud would bring in the claimed 6.7 billion pounds stg savings. One analyst said the unimportant tax changes have deflected attention from the fact that this has been a loose spending round.
-- ASBESTOSIS INSURANCE DEAL LIFTS T&N SHARES

The engineering group T&N reported a ground-breaking insurance deal and further provisions yesterday worth 1.2 billion pounds stg, as it attempts to leave behind its history as one of the world's biggest asbestos producers. Analysts had feared the group could be overwhelmed by a flood of personal injury suits from asbestosis sufferers. The plan will attempt to cap the group's liability to future claims.
-- MOORFIELD MAKES 214 MILLION POUNDS OFFER FOR GREYCOAT

The property company Moorfield Estates launched its bid for Greycoat yesterday, revealing detailed terms of an offer of 214 million pounds stg for Greycoat, which owns Embankment Place, the office development near Charing Cross station in London. The bid is made up of Moorfield shares and loan notes and will give Greycoat shareholders the net asset value of their holdings.
